---
title: "3.3 External Pull-Down Resistors"
description: "Use a resistor to establish a low state while an open switch disconnects the positive rail."
sidebar: tej
toc: true
execute: {enabled: false}
---

A pull-down resistor connects the input weakly to ground. The input reads low while the switch is open. Closing the switch connects the input to $V_{CC}$ and produces a high state.

![A switch connects a GPIO input to VCC while a resistor pulls the open input to ground.](/assets/tej/External_Pull_Down_Input.svg){fig-alt="A GPIO input is connected through a pull-down resistor to ground and through a normally open switch to VCC." width=90%}

::: {.table-responsive}
| Switch | Connection | Voltage | Logic | Active? |
|:--|:--|:--|:--:|:--|
| open | through $R_{PD}$ to ground | about $0\ \mathrm{V}$ | 0 | inactive |
| closed | to $V_{CC}$ | about $V_{CC}$ | 1 | active |
:::

The GPIO input draws very little current. The pull-down supplies a defined idle state without significantly loading the signal.

## Verification

1. Predict both states.
2. Calculate any current path that exists when the switch closes.
3. Draw the schematic with a junction dot at the input node.
4. Verify pin voltage for both states.
5. Disconnect the resistor and document the floating-input limitation.
